purpose: Zileuton is used to help prevent and manage asthma symptoms in adults and children 12 years and older. It helps reduce wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and coughing. It is a long-term controller medicine, not a rescue inhaler for sudden attacks.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called leukotrienes that cause swelling and tightening in your airways when you have asthma. Zileuton blocks an enzyme called 5-lipoxygenase, which stops your body from making those harmful chemicals. This helps keep your airways more open and reduces inflammation so breathing is easier.
common_side_effects: Headache, upset stomach, nausea, and generally feeling unwell are the most common side effects. Some people may notice elevated liver enzymes, which is why regular blood tests are needed. Sinus problems or a runny nose can also occur.
warnings: Zileuton can affect your liver, so your doctor will need to check your liver function with blood tests before you start and regularly while you take it. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, or extreme tiredness. It can also interact with several medications including warfarin and theophylline, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medicines you take. Do not use it as a rescue inhaler during an asthma attack. Some people may experience mood changes or depression — contact your doctor if this happens.
typical_dosing: The immediate-release tablet (Zyflo) is usually taken 4 times a day with or without food. The extended-release tablet (Zyflo CR) is typically taken twice a day within one hour after morning and evening meals. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not crush or chew the extended-release tablets.
